title: Physicists directly observe quantum gravity effects on ultracold atoms
summary: Researchers directly observed a quantum effect of gravity predicted by Einstein using ultracold atoms split between a held position and free fall.

title: Roivant lung disease drug achieves mid-stage trial success
summary: Roivant's experimental drug mosliciguat met primary endpoints in a Phase 2 trial for pulmonary hypertension, showing a 56% reduction in pulmonary vascular resistance versus placebo. The results exceeded expectations and position the drug as a potential new therapeutic approach and possible second bl
takeaways: 56% placebo-adjusted reduction in pulmonary vascular resistance
35-meter placebo-adjusted improvement in six-minute walk distance
53% placebo-adjusted reduction in NT-proBNP, a heart failure marker
16-week Phase 2 trial achieved primary and secondary endpoints

title: Researchers discover potent antivenom from rattlesnake blood proteins
summary: Scientists found that combinations of toxin-blocking proteins naturally present in rattlesnake blood are about 10 times more effective than current commercial antivenoms.

title: Semaglutide linked to 21% lower psychiatric hospitalization risk in bipolar disorder
summary: A large Swedish study of nearly 15,000 people with bipolar disorder found that semaglutide use (Ozempic, Wegovy) was associated with a 21% lower risk of psychiatric hospitalization.

title: Novartis Cardiovascular Drug Fails Pivotal Study
summary: Novartis announced September 4, 2026, that pelacarsen, an experimental cardiovascular drug, failed its pivotal Phase 3 HORIZON trial. Despite earlier success in lowering Lp(a) levels, the drug did not reduce cardiovascular death or acute cardiovascular events compared to placebo.
takeaways: Phase 3 HORIZON trial failed September 4, 2026
Earlier trials showed pelacarsen significantly lowered Lp(a), a lipid-protein linked to heart disease
Failed to reduce risk of cardiovascular death or acute events (heart attacks, stroke) vs. placebo
Competitors Amgen and Eli Lilly also developing Lp(a)-targeting therapies

title: Immune receptor blocking may reverse aging in mice
summary: Stanford Medicine researchers found that blocking a single immune receptor on tissue-resident macrophages restored their ability to clear senescent neutrophils, reducing inflammation and maintaining youthful function across multiple organs in aged mice. The intervention protected mice from frailty,
takeaways: Blocking single immune receptor restored cellular cleanup in tissue macrophages
Effects observed across brain, heart, skeletal muscle, liver, spleen, kidney, and colon
Protected mice from frailty, excess fat, and heart trouble
Substantially reduced cognitive decline in aged mice
Published in Science with Katrin Andreasson as senior author

title: Vesper bats possess unique dual antibody gene system enabling virus tolerance
summary: Scientists at Tulane University discovered that over 500 species of vesper bats possess two separate sets of antibody genes, an arrangement never before found in any mammal. The dual heavy-chain gene system may enable bats to create a wider variety of antibodies and help explain how they tolerate vi
takeaways: Over 500 vesper bat species carry dual antibody gene systems
First discovery of dual heavy-chain gene systems in any mammal
May enable wider antibody variety for viral tolerance
Published in Science Advances on September 3, 2026
Led by Hannah Frank at Tulane University

title: Ionis wins FDA approval for Zanvastro, first disease-modifying treatment for Alexander disease
summary: The FDA approved Zanvastro, the first disease-modifying therapy for Alexander disease, a rare and fatal neurological disorder. In the pivotal trial, walking speed remained stable in treated patients while the control group declined 33%, with hints that early treatment in young children could improve
takeaways: First disease-modifying therapy for Alexander disease
Walking speed stable in treated patients vs. 33% decline in control group
Approved for use in children and adults
Serious adverse events more common in control group than treated patients

title: ARPA-H invests $62 million in FDA-authorized AI for heart failure treatment
summary: ARPA-H committed $62.7 million to develop FDA-authorized AI systems for heart failure treatment through the ADVOCATE program. The initiative targets 6.7 million Americans with heart failure, particularly in underserved rural areas, with AI agents to assess symptoms, prescribe drugs, and order tests.
takeaways: $62.7 million total investment
$33.7 million in first-year awards to Atman Health, UpDoc, Tempus AI, Stanford, Duke, Kaiser Permanente
Up to $29 million additional funding available
Targets 6.7 million Americans with heart failure

title: Early statin use linked to 15% lower dementia risk in type 2 diabetes patients
summary: A Danish study of over 132,000 people found that starting statins within a year of type 2 diabetes diagnosis reduced dementia risk by 15% over 10 years.

title: AstraZeneca's experimental COPD drug shows strong late-stage trial results
summary: AstraZeneca's experimental COPD treatment demonstrated competitive efficacy in late-stage clinical studies with potential market differentiation.

title: Inhibrx achieves first success for long-elusive immunotherapy target
summary: Inhibrx reported the first positive result for a previously difficult immunotherapy target despite repeated failures in the field.

title: Researchers Identify New Weakness in Treatment-Resistant Prostate Cancer
summary: Scientists discovered a strategy to attack treatment-resistant prostate cancers by targeting cells that evade therapy through identity changes.

title: Immune Signal Discovered That Promotes Spinal Cord Regeneration
summary: Researchers have identified a neutrophil-derived immune signal (IL-4) that suppresses inflammation and enables spinal cord nerve fibers to regrow in zebrafish models.

title: Lifestyle program improves cognition 55% more than basic health advice
summary: A two-year study of older adults at dementia risk across 11 Latin American countries found that structured lifestyle programs combining exercise, diet, cognitive training, and social engagement produced 55% greater cognitive improvements than standard health advice. The program's success stemmed fro
takeaways: 55% greater cognitive improvement versus general health advice
Two-year LatAm-FINGERS study across 11 Latin American countries
Combines exercise, healthy eating, cognitive training, social engagement
Results published in The Lancet; presented at AAIC 2026 London
Strongest benefits with regular coaching and structured support
Culturally adapted: salsa/tango, MIND diet with avocado/quinoa/chia

title: Researchers identify vulnerability in glioblastoma cancer defenses
summary: Researchers at Ohio State University identified the SET protein as a therapeutic target in glioblastoma, finding that blocking it restores PP2A enzyme activity and increases cancer cells' sensitivity to radiation in preclinical models. An FDA-approved antipsychotic drug showed potential to enhance t
takeaways: SET protein blocks PP2A enzyme activity in glioblastoma cells
Blocking SET increased radiation sensitivity in lab and animal models
FDA-approved antipsychotic drug candidate may enhance PP2A activity
Approach designed to enhance existing radiation and chemotherapy, not replace them
Results are preliminary; human testing required

sources.label: ScienceDaily / Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center

title: Cancer cells hidden behind protective shields evade chemotherapy
summary: Researchers mapped breast tumors and discovered dormant cancer cells sheltered within protective barriers of immune and connective tissue cells. These quiescent cells survive chemotherapy by entering a hibernation-like state and can later reactivate to cause relapse, suggesting future treatments mus
takeaways: Dormant cancer cells survive chemotherapy and hide from treatment
Protected by surrounding immune and connective tissue cells
Can reactivate later to drive relapse and cancer spread
Study published in Genome Medicine from Imperial College London and UCL
Future therapies must target both active and dormant cells plus protective tissue environment

title: Seattle scientists launch $95 million AI biology research initiative
summary: Seattle-based researchers led by Nobel laureate David Baker announced $95 million in funding for an AI biology research initiative aimed at mapping nature's design rules using artificial intelligence.
takeaways: $95 million funding for AI biology research initiative
Led by Nobel laureate David Baker
Focus on using AI to map nature's design rules

title: Cambridge team led by Iraqi researcher achieves breakthrough in pancreatic cancer research
summary: A Cambridge University research team led by an Iraqi researcher has achieved a significant breakthrough in pancreatic cancer research.

title: Opinion: Autonomous AI Will Outperform Physician-Assisted Care by 2030
summary: Ezekiel J. Emanuel and Abe Baker-Butler argue that autonomous AI systems will surpass both unaided physicians and human-AI collaborative teams on core medical tasks within five years.

title: AI Falls Short in Emergency Rooms Despite Lofty Corporate Promises
summary: AI systems underperform expectations in real-world emergency department chaos, despite tech CEOs' predictions of eliminating cancer and transforming healthcare.

title: Pancreatic cancer patients struggle to access newly approved Rasonque drug
summary: Despite FDA approval of the new pancreatic cancer drug Rasonque, some patients face barriers in obtaining access to the breakthrough treatment.

title: Novo Nordisk halts two cardiovascular trials of inflammation-targeting drug
summary: Novo Nordisk discontinued two clinical trials of a drug designed to reduce inflammation and improve cardiovascular health outcomes.

title: High blood tyrosine linked to shorter male lifespan in large study
summary: Researchers found that elevated blood tyrosine levels are associated with reduced life expectancy in men, based on a study of over 270,000 people.

title: Study finds ADHD linked to creative advantage through defocused attention patterns
summary: Research suggests that defocused attention patterns characteristic of ADHD may enhance creativity by enabling broader exploration of ideas and unexpected connections.

title: FDA TEMPO pilot accelerates generative AI medical device authorization
summary: The FDA's TEMPO pilot program allows generative AI medical devices to reach patients before full marketing authorization, with Cadence and Limbic among early entrants.

title: Drug overdose deaths decline as naloxone and harm reduction efforts expand
summary: A new report indicates that naloxone availability and harm reduction measures are contributing to declining drug overdose mortality rates.

title: Prolonged Sitting Linked to 9% Higher Cancer Mortality Risk
summary: Research shows uninterrupted sedentary periods carry greater cancer mortality risk than equivalent time in shorter sitting bouts.

title: Pennsylvania measles outbreak claims two infants; coroner confirms virus as cause
summary: Two infants died in Pennsylvania from measles-related complications during a growing outbreak, with the virus confirmed as the direct cause of one death.

title: Sorbitol sugar substitute may convert to fructose in liver
summary: Researchers found that sorbitol, a common sugar alcohol in low-calorie foods, can be converted to fructose in the liver with potentially similar metabolic effects.

title: New Guidelines Target Heart-Kidney Disease Interaction
summary: New clinical guidelines recommend early screening and proven therapies to prevent heart and kidney diseases from accelerating one another.

title: Prenatal Joint Development May Predispose to Rheumatoid Arthritis
summary: Scientists discovered that finger joints commonly affected by rheumatoid arthritis develop with distinct tissue structures and larger fibroblast populations before birth.

title: AMA CEO: AI Will Augment Rather Than Replace Physicians
summary: American Medical Association CEO John Whyte argues that AI should complement rather than displace physicians in healthcare delivery.

title: HHS reverses position on disability lawsuit; overdose deaths decline
summary: The Department of Health and Human Services changed its stance on a disability-related lawsuit as part of broader health policy developments.

title: American Diabetes Association continues turbulence after June member ejections
summary: Five members ejected from the American Diabetes Association's June conference remain under review as the organization faces ongoing internal crisis.

title: Reader Opinion on AI in Medicine: Responsibility Cannot Be Transferred Via Physician Signature
summary: STAT reader opinion argues that physicians should not be able to magically transfer responsibility to themselves through mere signature or brief review of AI-generated outputs.

title: Mass General Brigham Medicare Advantage plan drops Dana-Farber Cancer Hospital
summary: Dana-Farber Cancer Hospital was dropped from Mass General Brigham's Medicare Advantage network following the health systems' earlier split.

title: Experts retain hope in alternative therapies after Angelman syndrome drug failure
summary: Following the failure of an experimental Angelman syndrome treatment, researchers remained optimistic about prospects for similar candidate therapies.
